  "text": "He turned without moving his feet. From the third step he could see the cupboard door, but not what stood behind it.

“How did you get down?”

“Give the ring to the boy.”

The boy stopped counting. He had arranged the coins in little towers, leaving a space between the silver and the copper.

“Don't give him anything else,” the woman said.

Upstairs, a floorboard creaked above his head.

He put the ring on the banister. It lay flat on the broad wooden knob, an ordinary thing in a place where someone might forget it.

“Anne, come out where I can see you.”

“I can't while she's here.”

The woman bent and pulled at the split in her shoe. There was a small stone inside. She took it out and placed it beside the money.

“That isn't what we agreed,” she said.

“I didn't agree. You told me.”

He knew that tone. His wife had used it with the man who fitted the kitchen, standing among the unconnected pipes with the estimate in her hand.

He stepped down.

The boy caught his sleeve.

“She'll need the ring first.”

“Which one?” he asked.

The boy looked upstairs.

Above them, someone crossed the landing. The steps were slow, with a pause between each one, as though the person walking had to be reminded how.

He reached for the ring.

It was no longer on the banister.

From the cupboard his wife began to cry, quietly and with evident annoyance, as she did when an injury prevented her from finishing something."
